The paper presents a method for measuring the RCS of objects at terahertz frequencies using a time-domain system.
The authors demonstrate the technique on a scale model of an F-16 aircraft.
The results are consistent with conventional radar measurements.
The method allows for the identification of scattering points.
The shape and positions of reflecting parts are retrieved by the filtered back projection algorithm.
The THz radiation is generated by optical rectification in lithium niobate crystal applying the tilted pulse front method.
The dynamic range of the THz generation setup is up to 43 dB.
The resolution of the THz beam is 73 mm of the THz electric field at the object distance.
The angle between the incident and scattered radiation is 6.6°.
The distance between the target and the detector is 1430 mm.
The smallest detectable sphere in a single scan is 0.98 mm diameter.
The frequency-averaged RCS is calculated using Eq. (2).
The RCS of a conducting sphere is equal to its physical cross-section area.
The RCS of a flat conducting plate decreases rapidly with angle from the maximum value.
The RCS should ideally be a parameter describing the target and should not depend on the target-detector distance.
The RCS of a circular flat disc reaches 91% of its long-distance value at a distance R=3r2/λ.
The longest THz waves generated in the setup have a wave vector of k=2π/λ=~2 mm−1 (at ~0.1 THz).
The target objects are placed on a support column of polystyrene foam with a low refractive index of 1.02 in the THz range.
